body: It looks like it might be related to comma-first style. (2 extra spaces would match comma+space)
I agree, but the `key-spacing` rule shouldn't care where the comma is placed as long as the parameter name and colons line up.

I think the problem is that we assume the lines are on the same level of indentation, which in your case they are not.  If your indentation is not consistent, it's very hard to do any vertical aligning.

Perhaps the solution is to include whitespace characters of the indentation when calculating alignment, rather than starting from the first non-whitespace character?

That's part of the problem, the assumption that the indent level is where the parameter name starts but not limited to. It seems to assume the parameter name is the length from the first non-whitespace character.

Using the npm coding style: https://docs.npmjs.com/misc/coding-style#comma-first is even worse.
e.g.

``` js
var obj = { foo : foo  // Extra space after key "foo".
          , bar : bar  // Missing space after key "bar".
          , cats: cats // Missing space after key "cats".
};
```

No errors:

``` js
var obj = { foo: foo
          , bar          : bar
          , cats         : cats
};
```
@BYK @btmills any ideas if this is something we want to fix and how hard would it be?

My hunch is that this not being too hard to fix (and I think this is something we should fix). I'm way behind my e-mail and ESLint stuff though so can't promise a timely patch. Will see what I can do over the weekend (or close to it).

Very well, accepted. I'm not positive, but [`getFirstNodeInLine`](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/rules/key-spacing.js#L106) seems like a pretty good place to start looking for the culprit.
